title: Knowledge check: Exploring a Vue Project

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Exploring a Vue Project”?
options: The dist/ folder is the editable source of the app.
Vite reads production secrets from client code.
The entry point creates the Vue app, registers features, and mounts the root component.
Every component must call createApp separately.
questions.answer_key: The entry point creates the Vue app, registers features, and mounts the root component.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Exploring a Vue Project directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “src , public , and project configuration”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Vite reads production secrets from client code.
The entry point creates the Vue app, registers features, and mounts the root component.
Every component must call createApp separately.
The dist/ folder is the editable source of the app.
questions.answer_key: The entry point creates the Vue app, registers features, and mounts the root component.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “src , public , and project configuration”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Exploring a Vue Project” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.

review_note: Answer keys and explanations are server-side data. Human review required before publication.
